evidence: Most plural/all/only/exactly-one wording is graded over the whole collection. Examples: constraints gate 'exactly one card for that candidate in Applied' (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23). hro_job_open covers all four invalid openings: blank, 0, 51 and 2.5 (functional/judge.toml:29). hro_activity says 'filtering to one job shows all of that job's lines and only those' (judge.toml:263). hro_activity_refusals says 'none of the refused attempts in this review added a line' (judge.toml:272), backed by protocol A 'Check that the refused attempts above added no line' (prompt.md:47). hro_undo_restores names W, X and Y and their original places (judge.toml:236). hro_bulk_all_or_none and hro_bulk_places use 'none of the set moves' / 'none moves' (judge.toml:218,227). hro_candidate_private requires 'no response a candidate page receives', with protocol K 'Capture every request the candidate page makes and inspect every response' (prompt.md:41). hro_anonymous says 'all refused' over five listed replays (judge.toml:191). hro_thread_earlier says 'until none remain' (judge.toml:326). hro_restart covers 'jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages and activity lines' (judge.toml:407). Most 'unchanged' guards are scoped to the refused action. Functional prompt.md:19 says 'A refused action may add a generic log line but must not change any card, order, message, note or activity entry'. pol_live_board fails only if the update 'resets scroll' (polish/judge.toml:23), not on any pixel change, so a legitimate layout reflow is not punished. DEFECT (one instance found): hro_unread_counts (functional/judge.toml:335) requires 'Mei Lin starts with 2 unread on Tomas Varga's Data Analyst conversation'. Protocol U places that read 'Before acting' (prompt.md:39), but U runs after M, L, C, B and T. In T, Mei Lin already uses the Conversations view: 'As Mei Lin write in Tomas's conversation' (prompt.md:37). Tomas has two conversations by then, the seeded Data Analyst one (APP-201) and the new J2 one, so the phrase is ambiguous. Under hireops_rules.md section 6 (Unread), having a conversation open at its newest message legitimately sets Mei's count to 0. Rafael's messages there would also legitimately raise it. Either happens if the judge picks APP-201 in T, or if the app auto-opens a conversation when the Conversations view loads. Auto-open is a layout choice the brief leaves open ('layout and names are yours'). The golden auto-opens only for single-thread candidates (threads.js:220), so the golden is unaffected. A seeded starting-state assertion is checked after steps that can legitimately change it. This conflicts with the task's own line 'never rely on starting counts' (prompt.md:15) and the template rule 'never mutate a record that a later criterion needs' (template functional/prompt.md:58-59). NOTES (not blocking for this row): (a) hro_bulk_move/arrive_bottom grade 'board order', but every bulk set in protocol B comes from a single stage. The rule 'by stage in the order listed above, then by place' for cards drawn from several stages (hireops_rules.md section 3, Moving several together) is never exercised, so an app that orders only by place passes. This is coverage, not a false-fail. (b) hro_pol_failed_send requires 'nothing was added to the conversation' (polish/judge.toml:50). An app that also shows a local 'not sent - retry' bubble while keeping the text in the box could be read as 'added'. The fail clause ('lost, shown as sent, or sent twice') mitigates this. (c) prompt.md:19 'may add a generic log line' is more lenient than rules section 4 ('A refused action adds no entry'). That is leniency, not a whole-collection gap. (d) Cross-dimension contamination of Mei's count by polish rows (failed_send and session_resume use an unspecified conversation and sign in as Mei) is unlikely. Scored dims run sequentially and, per the historical rewardkit copy, are discovered in sorted order (functional first). The image's rewardkit order is unverified. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope), so this is a static finding.
counterexample: Take a fully conforming HireOps whose staff Conversations view auto-selects the first listed conversation, sorted by job title so 'Data Analyst' comes first. Alternatively, a judge reads T's 'As Mei Lin write in Tomas's conversation' as Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation. Either way Mei has APP-201 open at its newest message during protocol T, so her unread count there correctly becomes 0, or 1+ after Rafael's later posts. In U the judge reads 0 and fails hro_unread_counts (weight 2 of the functional sum), even though the rules require exactly that count. A broken app that never records reads would still show 2 and pass this leg.
suggested_fix: Have protocol S (or a dedicated first step) read Mei Lin's seeded Data Analyst unread count before Mei signs in anywhere else. In T, say explicitly 'the new J2 conversation for Tomas' and forbid Mei from opening the Data Analyst conversation before U.
